title: Kestrel Retail - POC cost & benchmark kickoff

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19T15:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Khan (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Ava Li (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Kestrel H of ML), Marcus Reed (Kestrel CTO), Priya Shah (Kestrel Eng Manager), Omar Aziz (Kestel security)

Auto-summary: kickoff for cost/latency POC, cover workload sizing, thresholds, bench plan, and compliance asks.

[00:00] Samira: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro, this is our kickoff to scope the cost bench and POC. we want to make sure we're aligned on success criteria and the workload you'll run.
[00:18] Lena: thanks, yeah we wanna validate two things: one, the per-user cost for the recommendation chat flow and two, p95/p99 latency under holiday peak. if both are within our thresholds we proceed to a 3-month pilot.
[00:33] Diego: great, can you walk through current traffic and typical request shape? that helps us pick models and batching strategies.
[00:40] Priya: sure - basic numbers: about 10k MAU, roughly 3k active/day on the chat widget, average RPS about 4-6 during business hours and peaks up to 50 RPS on promo days. average input prompt is ~120 tokens, model output ~280 tokens so approx 400 tokens per request.
[01:05] Samira: ok that token profile is super helpful. so ballpark tokens/day ~ 1.2M on active days, average throughput low, peaks matter. what's your current latency SLO?
[01:15] Marcus: we want p95 < 350ms for the in-flow recommendation, p99 ideally < 600ms. Anything higher causes drop off in the UI.
[01:26] Diego: noted. for those SLOs we typically map model choices & quantization to expected token throughput and latency. if we use an opt-model ~13B quant-4 we can hit the latency targets with aggressive batching, but we'll explore medium/large models too for quality.
[01:44] Lena: quality matters — we need click-through lift on recommendations, so the success criteria will be CTR delta > 7% vs baseline and latency constraints met.
[01:56] Ava: on caching — have you looked at session prefix caching? keeping a small KV cache for user context can reduce repeated prompt tokens by 15-30% depending on your UX.
[02:08] Priya: we do session context client-side but we still send problem history to the model. if caching can reduce token bills that's big for our budget.
[02:16] Diego: for the POC we recommend enabling prefix/KV cache and a two-tier batching strategy: small ultra-low-latency path (no batching or micro-batch up to 2 reqs with 5-10ms window) for interactive flows, and a autoscaled batch path for background/bulk requests. that typically reduces per-token compute cost by 20-40% depending on workload shape.
[02:37] Samira: to make this concrete, we ran a quick estimate: assuming average 400 tokens/request, 6 RPS baseline, that equals ~2.4k tokens/sec. Using an Llama-13B-4bit path on Redwood hosted, we estimate per-token compute cost range ~$0.0000018 - $0.0000035 depending on batching and kv hit rate. so per-request compute cost ~ $0.00072 - $0.0014. with other infra and margin, per-request landed cost ~ $0.0012 - $0.0022.
[03:15] Marcus: that's helpful, can you break down the variables? e.g., peak vs avg and effect of cache hit rate?
[03:22] Diego: yes so main knobs: batch size/latency window, cache hit rate (prefix or KV cache), model quant/profile (4bit vs 8bit, or smaller model), and routing to dedicated vs hosted instances. higher cache hit reduces tokens processed, batching reduces kernel overhead. for example, a 40% cache hit and moderate batching we move to the lower end of your per-token range.
[03:49] Lena: any thoughts on using a dedicated pool vs hosted? we have compliance concerns and predictable throughput needs during promotions.
[03:56] Ava: Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and more predictable latency under burst; it costs more in committed spend but reduces variance and can lower per-token unit cost at scale. Hosted is faster to launch and cheaper for proof-of-concept but can have slightly wider tail latency during noisy neighbor events. we can also provide a hybrid: hosted for baseline and reserved for promo windows.
[04:18] Omar: on compliance — do you support our KMS and SAML SSO? we need to confirm log retention and audit hooks.
[04:24] Samira: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations, SAML/SSO, and audit logs. for hosted we have encryption at rest and in transit, and we can provide SOC2 docs; we'll include a security pack in the follow-ups.
[04:36] Priya: back to bench — what's the concrete bench plan? what will you run and what metrics will we get?
[04:42] Diego: plan is synthetic replay of your traces at three tiers: small (baseline day), medium (typical peak), and large (promo peak). we'll run model variants: 7B-4bit, 13B-4bit, and a 70B quant-lite if you want to test best quality. metrics captured: tokens/sec, GPU utilization, p50/p95/p99 latencies, cost per token, end-to-end throughput, and estimated monthly cost. we'll also test caching on/off to show delta.
[05:10] Samira: timeline — we propose bench in next week, analysis the following week, and an internal decision meeting the week after. so bench runs by 11/25, results review 11/29, go/no-go by 12/3. does that align?
[05:23] Marcus: yes that lines up. we need the pricing workbook to run finance approval too.
[05:29] Samira: will send pricing sheet with scenario lines: hosted small, hosted + caching, dedicated reserved (monthly commit) with break-even point.
[05:37] Lena: one more thing — we track token leakage concerns (PII). can we scrub traces and run an eval for leakage?
[05:45] Diego: yes we can run a privacy scrub step on the traces before replay and include a simple leakage check. Omar, we'd like your checklist to ensure we're aligned on scrub rules.
[05:53] Omar: I will send a short questionnaire and minimal compliance list.
[05:57] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[06:00] Priya: ok final recap?
[06:02] Samira: quick recap: Redwood runs synthetic benches on your traces (3 tiers) across 3 model configs, we test caching and batching knobs, deliver a bench report with p95/p99 lat and cost curves. Samira sends pricing + security pack; Kestrel shares anonymized traces and security checklist. follow-up meeting week of 11/29.
[06:21] Marcus: thanks all, excited to see the numbers.
[06:24] Lena: thanks, bye.

Notes on imperfect transcription: some proper nouns and acronyms transcribed variably (SOC2 spelled as SOC two, KV cache sometimes KV cash). references: shared pricing workbook (link: drive.redwood/poc-pricing-kestrel) and bench template (link: drive.redwood/bench-template).
